examples.ko: 나라의 교육 제도를 선진화해야 한다는 목소리가 커요.
examples.en: There are growing calls to modernize the country's education system.
They increased research funding to advance the industry.
There were many difficulties in the process of advancement.
The government promised to advance the medical system.

examples.ko: 교통의 선진화가 도시를 더 편하게 만들어요.
examples.en: Advancing transportation makes the city more convenient.
It takes a long time for advancement to be achieved.

explain: 제도, 산업, 기술, 시스템이 선진국 수준으로 발전하는 것을 말해서 뉴스나 정책 이야기에 많이 나와요. 사람에게는 쓰지 않고, 일상에서는 '발전하다'처럼 더 쉬운 말을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It means systems, industries and technology reaching the level of developed countries, so it shows up in news and policy talk. It is not used for people, and in daily speech simpler words like '발전하다' are often used.

examples.ko: 송유관에서 기름이 새서 큰 사고가 났어요.
examples.en: Oil leaked from the pipeline and caused a big accident.
This oil pipeline runs under the sea.
I saw news about the pipeline construction on TV.

examples.ko: 두 나라를 잇는 송유관이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new oil pipeline connecting the two countries was built.

examples.ko: 송유관이 터지면 주변 땅이 많이 오염돼요.
examples.en: If a pipeline bursts, the surrounding land gets badly polluted.

examples.ko: 공장 옆으로 긴 송유관이 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: A long oil pipeline runs alongside the factory.

explain: 뉴스에서 '송유관 폭발', '송유관 건설'처럼 사고나 나라 사이의 에너지 문제와 함께 자주 나와요. 가스를 보내는 관은 '가스관'이라고 하니 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: In the news it appears in phrases like '송유관 폭발' and '송유관 건설', often about accidents or energy issues between countries. A pipe that carries gas is called '가스관', so it is good to learn them as a pair.

examples.en: In the old days, soldiers plundered villages.
The thieves looted the store and ran away.
Plundering cultural property is a serious wrong.

examples.ko: 해적들이 배를 습격해서 물건을 약탈했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say pirates attacked ships and plundered the goods.

examples.ko: 사람들이 약탈할 수 없게 문을 단단히 잠갔어요.
examples.en: We locked the doors tight so people couldn't loot the place.
Things that were looted must be returned later.

explain: '훔치다'는 몰래 가져가는 것이고, '약탈하다'는 힘으로 여럿이 크게 빼앗는 것이에요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스와 역사 이야기에서 써요.
explain_en: 훔치다 is taking something secretly; 약탈하다 is taking things by force, often on a large scale. You meet it in news and history rather than everyday chat.

examples.en: The government decided to weaken the regulations.
The controversy grew after the rules were weakened.
That incident weakened trust in the company.

examples.ko: 너무 많은 규칙은 선수의 자율성을 약화할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Too many rules can weaken a player's autonomy.
Frequent quarrels weaken teamwork.

examples.ko: 새 규칙이 시험의 의미를 약화한다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think the new rule weakens the meaning of the exam.

explain: '약화하다'는 어떤 것을 일부러, 또는 결과적으로 약하게 만든다는 뜻으로 주로 써요. 저절로 약해질 때는 '약화되다'나 '약해지다'가 자연스러워요. 반대말은 '강화하다'예요. 뉴스, 글말에서 주로 나와요.
explain_en: '약화하다' mainly means making something weaker, on purpose or as a result. When something weakens by itself, '약화되다' or '약해지다' sounds more natural. Its opposite is '강화하다', and it appears mostly in news and writing.

examples.en: A chain reaction occurred and the problem grew.

examples.ko: 한 가게가 닫자 연쇄적 폐업이 이어졌어요.
examples.en: When one shop closed, a string of closures followed.
The blackout spread one after another to several neighborhoods.

examples.ko: 연쇄적인 사고를 막으려면 원인부터 찾아야 해요.
examples.en: To prevent a series of accidents, you must find the cause first.

examples.ko: 작은 실수가 연쇄적으로 큰 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: A small mistake snowballed into a big problem.
Consumers are struggling with the successive price hikes.

explain: 사슬처럼 서로 이어져서 잇따라 일어나는 일에 써요. 단순히 '계속'이 아니라 앞의 일이 뒤의 일을 불러온다는 느낌이 있어요. 관형사로 표시됐지만 '연쇄적인', '연쇄적으로'로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is for things that link like a chain and happen one after another. It is not just 'continuous'; the earlier event triggers the next. It is labeled a determiner here, but it is also commonly used as '연쇄적인' and '연쇄적으로'.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 오랫동안 외세의 간섭을 받았어요.
examples.en: This country was under foreign interference for a long time.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 외세와 싸운 영웅들을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, we learned about heroes who fought foreign powers.

examples.ko: 외세에 기대지 않고 스스로 일어서자는 말이 나왔어요.
examples.en: People said we should stand on our own without leaning on foreign powers.

examples.ko: 외세가 들어오면서 전통 문화가 많이 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: As foreign influence came in, traditional culture changed a lot.
That king tried to drive out foreign powers.

examples.ko: 외세는 힘이 약한 나라를 흔들곤 했어요.
examples.en: Foreign powers used to shake weak countries.

explain: 다른 나라의 힘이나 영향을 말하고, 주로 역사나 정치 글에서 간섭, 침략과 함께 나와서 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 그냥 외국을 말할 때는 '외국'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the power or influence of other countries and mostly appears in history or politics with words like interference and invasion, so it has a negative feel. For plain foreign countries, just say '외국'.

examples.en: This year it snowed more than ever before.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 유례없이 빠르게 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: That movie became popular at an unprecedented speed.
The government promised an unprecedentedly large amount of support.

examples.ko: 이번 대회에는 유례없이 많은 사람이 참가했어요.
examples.en: An unprecedented number of people took part in this competition.
It was a day when the market was unusually quiet, like never before.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 유례없이 짧은 시간에 일을 끝냈어요.
examples.en: Our team finished the work in an unprecedentedly short time.

explain: '많다, 빠르다, 크다'처럼 정도를 나타내는 말 앞에 와서 '지금까지 이런 적이 없을 만큼'이라는 느낌을 더해요. 일상 대화에서는 '역대급으로'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It goes before words of degree such as 많다, 빠르다 and 크다 to add the feeling of 'more than ever before'. In casual talk people also say '역대급으로'.

examples.ko: 인종주의가 사회에 아직 남아 있다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think racism still remains in society.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 인종주의에 반대하는 글을 많이 썼어요.
examples.en: That writer wrote many pieces against racism.
Education is important if we want to get rid of racism.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 인종주의 문제를 다룬 토론을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a debate on the news about the problem of racism.
That remark was criticized as racism.
I joined a citizens' group that stands up against racism.

explain: '인종 차별'은 차별하는 행동을 가리킬 때 많이 쓰고, '인종주의'는 그런 생각이나 이념을 말할 때 자연스러워요. '인종차별주의'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '인종 차별' is natural when you talk about discriminatory acts, while '인종주의' fits when you talk about the underlying ideas or ideology. '인종차별주의' is also used.

examples.en: Our country sets monogamy in law.
Do you think monogamy is a given?

examples.ko: 사회 시간에 일부일처제의 변화에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: In social studies, we learned about changes in monogamy.

examples.ko: 일부일처제는 오랫동안 이어져 온 결혼 제도예요.
examples.en: Monogamy is a marriage system that has lasted for a long time.

examples.ko: 어떤 나라에서는 일부일처제 대신 다른 결혼 형태도 인정해요.
examples.en: Some countries recognize other forms of marriage besides monogamy.

examples.ko: 이 책은 일부일처제와 가족의 관계를 다뤄요.
examples.en: This book deals with the relationship between monogamy and the family.

explain: 한 남편과 한 아내만 두는 결혼 제도를 말해요. 반대말은 '일부다처제'예요. 결혼 형태를 설명하는 사회, 역사 수업이나 글에서 많이 만나는 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to a marriage system with one husband and one wife only. The opposite is '일부다처제'. You meet it in social studies, history and writing that explains forms of marriage.

examples.en: Lawmaking is an important job of the National Assembly.

examples.ko: 새 법을 만드는 입법 과정을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned about the legislative process of making new laws.
Citizens are demanding new legislation.
Legislation takes longer than I thought.
The legislation was delayed, so the problem grew.

examples.ko: 입법과 행정은 서로 다른 일을 해요.
examples.en: Legislation and administration do different jobs.

explain: 입법은 법을 집행하는 '행정', 법으로 판단하는 '사법'과 짝으로 배워요. '입법 활동', '입법 과정', '입법부'처럼 뒤에 붙는 말과 함께 뉴스에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: 입법 is learned as a set with '행정' (administration, carrying out laws) and '사법' (the judiciary, judging by law). It appears in the news with words like '입법 활동', '입법 과정', and '입법부' (the legislature).

examples.en: The government announced import liberalization.
Prices rose after price liberalization.

examples.ko: 여행 자유화가 되자 해외에 나가는 사람이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Once travel was liberalized, more people went abroad.

examples.ko: 시장 자유화에 찬성하는 사람도 있고 반대하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people support market liberalization and some oppose it.
Farmers are worried because of the liberalization measures.
When was the exchange rate liberalized?

explain: '수입 자유화, 가격 자유화'처럼 앞에 분야를 붙여서 주로 뉴스와 경제 수업에서 나와요. 일상에서는 '규제를 풀다, 완화하다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It usually follows a field, as in '수입 자유화' or '가격 자유화', and appears mostly in news and economics classes. In everyday speech people often say '규제를 풀다' or '완화하다'.

en: remain; be still existent; be extant

examples.ko: 오래된 건물에는 아직도 옛날 흔적이 잔존해요.
examples.en: Traces of the past still remain in old buildings.
We tested whether any pesticide residue remains.

examples.ko: 잔존하는 문제가 있으면 먼저 알려 주세요.
examples.en: If there are any remaining problems, please tell me first.

examples.ko: 불씨가 잔존해 있을 수 있으니 끝까지 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: Embers may still be left, so you have to check until the end.

examples.ko: 병이 나은 뒤에도 약간의 통증이 잔존할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Some pain can remain even after the illness is gone.

examples.ko: 도시가 개발되면서 숲이 잔존한 곳은 얼마 없어요.
examples.en: As the city developed, there are few places where forest still remains.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '남아 있다'라고 많이 말하고, '잔존하다'는 뉴스나 보고서 같은 딱딱한 글에서 더 자주 보여요. '잔존 물질'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여서 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: In everyday talk people usually say '남아 있다' (to be left), while '잔존하다' shows up more in stiff writing like news and reports. It can also be placed before a noun, as in '잔존 물질' (residual substance).

examples.ko: 두 나라는 오랫동안 서로를 적국으로 여겼어요.
examples.en: The two countries regarded each other as enemy states for a long time.

examples.ko: 전쟁이 끝나자 적국이었던 나라와 다시 교류했어요.
examples.en: After the war ended, they resumed exchanges with the country that had been an enemy.

examples.ko: 옛이야기 속 장군은 적국의 왕을 사로잡았어요.
examples.en: In the old tale, the general captured the king of the enemy state.
There is a record that they sent a spy to the enemy state.

examples.ko: 적국이라고 해도 국민끼리는 사이가 좋을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even if countries are enemies, their citizens can get along.
That country negotiated secretly with an enemy state.

explain: '적'은 사람이나 팀에도 쓰지만, 적국은 전쟁이나 심한 갈등 상태에 있는 나라만 가리켜요. 반대로 사이가 좋은 나라는 '우방국', '동맹국'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '적' can refer to people or teams, but 적국 refers only to a country in war or serious conflict. Friendly countries are called '우방국' or '동맹국'.

examples.en: Economic dependence is growing steadily worse.

examples.ko: 한 회사에 대한 종속을 줄이려고 거래처를 늘렸어요.
examples.en: We added clients to reduce our dependence on a single company.
We learned about subordinate clauses in grammar class.

examples.ko: 하청 업체의 종속 구조가 문제라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the subordinate structure of subcontractors is a problem.
I worry about excessive dependence on machines.
Subordination and cooperation are completely different relationships.

explain: 종속은 힘이 약한 쪽이 강한 쪽에 매여 있는 상태에 써서 '독립'과 짝이에요. 경제나 정치 글, 문법 용어('종속절')에서 주로 봐요. 일상 말로는 '의존'이 부드럽지만, 종속은 스스로 결정하지 못한다는 점이 더 강해요.
explain_en: This describes a weaker side being tied to a stronger one, and it pairs with '독립' (independence). You see it in economics and politics writing and in grammar terms like '종속절' (subordinate clause). '의존' (reliance) is milder; '종속' stresses the inability to decide for yourself.

examples.ko: 그는 남의 말에 너무 쉽게 좌지우지돼요.
examples.en: He is pushed around too easily by what other people say.

examples.ko: 작은 소문에 좌지우지되지 말고 직접 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't be swayed by small rumors; check for yourself.

examples.ko: 회사의 운명이 한 사람의 결정에 좌지우지되면 위험해요.
examples.en: It's dangerous if a company's fate is controlled by one person's decision.

examples.ko: 저는 기분에 좌지우지되는 사람이 되고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to be someone who is ruled by my moods.

examples.ko: 시장이 몇몇 큰 회사에 좌지우지된다는 비판이 나와요.
examples.en: There is criticism that the market is controlled by a few big companies.

examples.ko: 친구한테 좌지우지돼서 하고 싶은 일을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was pushed around by my friend and couldn't do what I wanted.

explain: 보통 '-에 좌지우지되다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 써요. 남이 나를 마음대로 움직이는 건 '좌지우지하다'이고, 일상 대화에서는 '휘둘리다'도 비슷하게 말해요. 좋지 않은 상황을 말할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: It is usually used with the particle '에', as in '-에 좌지우지되다'. The active form '좌지우지하다' means to control someone as you like, and in everyday talk people also say '휘둘리다' in a similar way. It fits unwelcome situations.

examples.en: Because of the housing shortage, home prices are high in big cities.

examples.ko: 주택난이 심해서 신혼부부가 집 구하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The housing shortage is severe, so newlyweds struggle to find a home.

examples.ko: 정부가 주택난을 해결하려고 새 아파트를 지어요.
examples.en: The government is building new apartments to solve the housing shortage.
Even amid the housing shortage, monthly rent keeps rising.
That city has suffered from a housing shortage for a long time.
The housing shortage is a big worry for young people.

explain: '-난(難)'이 붙으면 '구하기 어려운 어려움'을 뜻해서 '취업난, 구인난, 식량난'처럼 써요. 주로 뉴스나 사회 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: The suffix '-난(難)' means difficulty in obtaining something, as in '취업난', '구인난' and '식량난'. This word mostly appears in news and discussions of social issues.

examples.en: The teacher called on me, and I was startled.
The police named that man as the culprit.

examples.ko: 저도 대답하고 싶으니까 저를 지목해 주세요.
examples.en: I want to answer too, so please call on me.
It's hard to point out who was at fault.

examples.ko: 전문가들이 가장 큰 원인으로 지목하는 것은 소음이에요.
examples.en: What experts point to as the biggest cause is noise.

examples.ko: 제가 지목할 사람은 바로 저 친구예요.
examples.en: The person I will pick is that friend over there.

explain: 여럿 가운데 한 사람이나 하나를 콕 집어 가리킬 때 써요. 수업에서 선생님이 학생을 부를 때, 뉴스에서 원인이나 범인을 짚을 때 자주 나와요. '가리키다'는 손가락으로 방향을 보이는 것이고, '지목하다'는 대상으로 정해서 말하는 거예요.
explain_en: Use it when you pick out one person or thing from a group. It shows up when a teacher calls on a student, and in the news when a cause or suspect is named. 가리키다 is pointing in a direction; 지목하다 is naming someone or something as the target.

examples.en: I heard my grandfather went off on forced labor service.

examples.ko: 강제 징용 문제가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: The forced labor draft issue often comes up in the news.

examples.ko: 책으로 징용에서 돌아온 사람들의 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a book about people who came back from the labor draft.
We learned about the labor draft in history class.

examples.ko: 증조할아버지는 징용으로 먼 곳에 끌려가셨다고 해요.
examples.en: They say my great-grandfather was taken far away by the labor draft.
The labor draft is a painful part of history from the Japanese colonial period.

explain: 일제강점기의 '강제 징용'처럼 나라가 사람들을 강제로 불러 일을 시킬 때 써요. 군인으로 불러 가는 것은 '징병'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 뉴스와 역사 수업에서 자주 들리고 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a state forcibly calls people up to work, as in the colonial-era '강제 징용'. Being called up as a soldier is '징병', so the two differ. You hear it in the news and history classes, but hardly in everyday talk.

examples.en: A typhoon is coming, so the company is on high alert.

examples.ko: 아이가 안 보여서 온 가족이 초비상이었어요.
examples.en: The child was missing, so the whole family was in a state of emergency.
It's the day before the exam, so even the library feels like an emergency.

examples.ko: 마감 때문에 팀 전체가 초비상에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: Because of the deadline, the entire team went on high alert.

examples.ko: 초비상 상황이라서 오늘은 아무도 퇴근 못 해요.
examples.en: It's an all-hands emergency, so nobody can leave work today.
When the flu spread, every school went on high alert.

explain: '비상'보다 훨씬 급하고 긴장된 상황이에요. 보통 '초비상이다', '초비상이 걸리다'로 쓰고, 말할 때는 회사나 집이 정신없이 바쁠 때도 조금 과장해서 써요.
explain_en: It describes a much more urgent and tense situation than '비상'. It usually appears as '초비상이다' or '초비상이 걸리다', and in speech people also use it with some exaggeration when a company or home is in a frantic rush.

examples.en: The conflict was triggered by a small misunderstanding.

examples.ko: 그 발언으로 논란이 촉발될 수 있어요.
examples.en: That remark could set off a controversy.
This protest was set off by the ruling.
A single mistake can set off a war.
My anxiety was set off and I couldn't sleep.
It is a situation in which emotions are easily set off.

explain: 일이 저절로 터져 나오는 느낌이에요. 주어는 갈등, 논란, 시위, 감정처럼 '벌어지는 일'이 와요. 누가 일으켰는지 말하고 싶으면 '촉발하다'를 써요. 사람이 주어로 오지는 않아요.
explain_en: It feels like something bursting out on its own. The subject is an event that breaks out, such as a conflict, controversy, protest, or emotion. When you want to say who caused it, use '촉발하다'. A person does not serve as the subject.

examples.ko: 영화에서 총격 장면이 나오자 아이가 눈을 가렸어요.
examples.en: When a gunfight scene came up in the movie, the child covered his eyes.
When the gunfire stopped, people came outside.

examples.ko: 게임 속에서 총격을 받고 캐릭터가 쓰러졌어요.
examples.en: In the game, my character was shot at and fell down.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 총격 장면이 너무 많아서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: That movie has too many shooting scenes, so it was scary.
A long gunfight broke out at the end of the movie.

examples.ko: 영화 속 총격 소리에 놀란 아이가 울기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The child, startled by the gunfire in the movie, began to cry.

explain: '총소리'는 소리 자체를 말하고, '총격'은 총을 쏘는 행위나 사건을 가리켜요. 뉴스에서 '총격 사건', '총격을 받다', '총격전'처럼 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: 총소리 is the sound of a gun; 총격 is the act or incident of shooting. In the news you see '총격 사건', '총격을 받다', and '총격전' a lot, but it's rare in daily conversation.

examples.en: Livestock farming is well developed in this region.
My father is in the livestock business.
The price of livestock products went up a lot.
He studied animal husbandry at university.
I hear livestock farmers have a lot of worries.
There was news about livestock farms on TV.

explain: 축산은 소, 돼지, 닭을 키워서 고기나 우유, 달걀을 얻는 일을 통틀어 말해요. 뉴스나 신문에서는 '축산업', '축산물', '축산 농가'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 자주 써요. 식물을 키우는 일은 '농사'나 '재배'라고 해서 구별해요.
explain_en: Chuksan is the general word for raising cattle, pigs, or chickens for meat, milk, and eggs. In news and papers it usually appears with a following word, as in 축산업, 축산물, and 축산 농가. Growing plants is called 농사 or 재배, so the two are kept apart.

examples.en: This road is closed to traffic because of construction.
A no-passage sign is posted at the entrance.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 산길은 통행금지가 됐어요.
examples.en: It snowed a lot, so the mountain road was closed.
I heard that in the old days there was a curfew every night.
You must not enter the restricted area.

examples.ko: 차량 통행금지라서 걸어서 갈 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: Cars are banned, so we have no choice but to walk.

explain: 길이나 구역으로 사람이나 차가 지나가지 못하게 막는다는 뜻으로, 표지판이나 안내문에서 많이 봐요. '차량 통행금지', '보행자 통행금지'처럼 대상을 앞에 붙여요. 옛날 한국에는 밤에 돌아다닐 수 없던 '야간 통행금지'도 있었어요.
explain_en: It means people or vehicles may not pass through a road or area, and you often see it on signs and notices. You put the target in front, as in '차량 통행금지' or '보행자 통행금지'. In Korea's past there was also a nighttime curfew called '야간 통행금지'.

en: step down; resign from a position

examples.en: The president took responsibility and stepped down.
The coach will step down when the season ends.
People are demanding that the CEO step down.
I hear the chairman will step down within this year.

examples.ko: 그 의원은 끝까지 퇴진하지 않겠다고 말했어요.
examples.en: That lawmaker said they would not step down no matter what.
Nobody knew why they were suddenly stepping down.

explain: '그만두다'는 누구에게나 쓰지만 '퇴진하다'는 사장, 감독, 대표처럼 높은 자리에서 물러날 때 써요. 일반 직원이나 학생에게는 어색해요. 뉴스에서 '퇴진을 요구하다'로 자주 보여요.
explain_en: 그만두다 works for anyone, but 퇴진하다 is for leaving a high post such as president, coach, or CEO. It sounds odd for an ordinary employee or student. In the news you often see '퇴진을 요구하다'.

examples.en: Other problems arise from this problem.
A big fight arose from a small misunderstanding.
There are many words derived from English words.

examples.ko: 새 서비스가 기존 앱에서 파생해 나왔어요.
examples.en: The new service branched off from the existing app.
You have to think about the knock-on effects that follow as well.
I worried about the consequences this decision would bring.

explain: 보통 '~에서 파생하다'로 쓰고, 하나에서 갈라져 나온 것에 써요. '생기다'보다 딱딱해서 글이나 보고서에서 많이 나와요. 국어에서 '파생어'는 '덮개'처럼 어근에 접사가 붙어 만든 말이에요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '~에서 파생하다', for something that branches off from one origin. It is stiffer than 생기다 and common in writing and reports. In Korean grammar, a 파생어 is a word formed by adding an affix to a root, like 덮개.

examples.en: The construction team demolished the old building with explosives.
In the movie, the hero blows up a bridge.
They will blast the rock to make a tunnel.
Everyone was evacuated before the blast.

examples.ko: 폭탄으로 건물을 폭파한 범인을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: They are searching for the criminal who blew up the building.

examples.ko: 낡은 굴뚝을 폭파하면 큰 소리가 나요.
examples.en: Blowing up an old chimney makes a loud noise.

explain: 폭탄이나 화약으로 건물, 다리, 바위처럼 큰 것을 터뜨려 부술 때 써요. '터뜨리다'는 풍선, 웃음, 울음에도 쓰지만 '폭파하다'는 큰 구조물에만 써요. 뉴스와 영화 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when blasting big things such as buildings, bridges, or rock with bombs or explosives. '터뜨리다' also works for balloons, laughter, and tears, but '폭파하다' is only for large structures. It is common in news and movie talk.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 합병 소식이 오늘 아침에 나왔어요.
examples.en: News of the merger of the two companies came out this morning.

examples.ko: 합병이 끝나면 부서도 새로 나뉠 거예요.
examples.en: Once the merger is finished, the departments will be divided anew.

examples.ko: 합병은 작은 회사에게 기회가 되기도 해요.
examples.en: A merger can also be an opportunity for a small company.

examples.ko: 회사는 합병을 앞두고 직원들에게 설명회를 했어요.
examples.en: Ahead of the merger, the company held a briefing for employees.
The merger created one big bank.

examples.ko: 저는 합병 뒤에 입사해서 옛날 이름을 몰라요.
examples.en: I joined after the merger, so I don't know the old name.

explain: 회사와 회사가 하나가 되는 일에 많이 써요. 인수는 한쪽이 다른 쪽을 사서 가져오는 것이고, 합병은 둘을 합쳐 하나로 만드는 거예요. 뉴스와 경제 이야기에 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used when one company becomes one with another. 인수 (acquisition) is when one side buys the other, while 합병 puts the two together as one. It comes up often in news and economy talk.

examples.ko: 지나친 게임은 아이들에게 해악이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Too much gaming can be harmful to children.

examples.ko: 거짓 정보는 사회에 큰 해악을 끼쳐요.
examples.en: False information does great harm to society.

examples.ko: 플라스틱의 해악은 바다에서 가장 크게 드러나요.
examples.en: The harm of plastic shows up most clearly in the ocean.

examples.ko: 스마트폰의 해악에 대한 연구가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: Research on the harms of smartphones is increasing.

examples.ko: 그 규칙은 이익보다 해악이 더 커요.
examples.en: That rule does more harm than good.

examples.ko: 해악 없는 방법을 찾아보는 게 좋겠어요.
examples.en: It would be good to look for a method that does no harm.

explain: '피해'가 입은 손해라면 '해악'은 해로운 영향이나 나쁜 것 자체에 가까워요. '해악을 끼치다'로 자주 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '나쁜 영향'이라고 풀어서 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: '피해' is the damage someone suffers, while '해악' is closer to the harmful influence or the bad thing itself. It is often used as '해악을 끼치다'. In daily talk people often say '나쁜 영향' (bad influence) instead.

examples.en: A hiker went missing in the mountains.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 어부 두 명이 행방불명됐대요.
examples.en: I heard two fishermen went missing because of the typhoon.
They are looking for the missing child.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 오 년 전에 행방불명됐다고 해요.
examples.en: They say he went missing five years ago.
If someone goes missing, you must contact the police right away.
The cat that left home is missing, and I'm worried.

explain: 사람이 어디 있는지 알 수 없게 된 상태예요. 물건이 안 보일 때는 쓰지 않고 '없어지다', '잃어버리다'를 써요. 뉴스에서는 '실종되다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 나오는데, 이쪽이 더 짧고 흔해요.
explain_en: It describes a person whose whereabouts are unknown. For objects you don't use it; say 없어지다 or 잃어버리다. In the news 실종되다 is the same idea and is shorter and more common.
